reproducibility_note: compile vs compile: the tier router reproduced (5/6 shared candidates same tier) but candidate mining did NOT (6 vs 21 regularities). Enforce extraction against a fixed regularity-class checklist before trusting reproducibility. See (lab notes)2026-06-18_compile_schema.md.

fences.rule: Every root table: id = text('id').primaryKey() as first column.
All Drizzle column PROPERTY KEYS are snake_case, universally (the standard). DB column-name string args were already snake_case.
fences.note: Landed via branch schema-money. Boundary mappers removed; snake_case is end-to-end (DB → API → web).

fences.rule: All money columns are bigint(mode:'number') integer cents — never numeric/float. Display ÷100; input ×100; Stripe boundary needs no conversion (payments.amount IS cents).
fences.note: Landed via branch schema-money (migration 0044+). amount_value is dual-unit: cents when amount_type='flat', basis-points when 'percent'.

fences.rule: HubSpot-mirror tables declare last_event_at NOT NULL default '-infinity'::timestamptz (H2 LWW guard).
fences.note: first compile placed this in assay (scope=intent); second compile placed it in wall — a wall/assay drift to pin.

fences.rule: status/type/kind columns use text(..., {enum:[...]}), not free text. Exception: contract_events.type (open taxonomy — see judge).
Enum columns carry a .default() that is a member of the enum.
created_at/updated_at use .notNull().defaultNow(); the H2 guard col is the withTimezone exception.
Pure join tables: 2 FK cols, composite primaryKey([a,b]), both cascade, no payload.
Portal access uses an unguessable token column (NOT NULL UNIQUE), never the PK, never sequential.

rubrics.rubric: Is this an audit/event table that no code path may UPDATE? (e.g. contract_events).
Should a new type column be open (free text) or closed (enum)? contract_events.type is deliberately open.
Should this child survive parent deletion? cascade vs set null vs none (payments deliberately omit cascade to preserve financial records).
Does any path mutate a contract version after sent_to_client_at? (must not — contracts immutable once generated).
Anchor table + immutable version table with version_number per parent — never mutate, always new version.
Is any file_key/artifact exposed via a public URL? (signatures must stay private).
Does this lifecycle table record WHO on each transition (actor_kind + created_by/updated_by)?
Is a discriminated-union column populated consistently with its tag? (e.g. days_before_event ⇔ due_date_type='days_before_event').

signs.prose: Lifecycle recorded as discrete nullable *_at timestamps vs a single status field — a modeling-taste choice.
Every table/column carries an explaining comment; deliberate divergences annotated inline. Presence is checkable; usefulness is not.
